clue.text: Extra earnings for mistress

definitions.meaning: money made from a sideline, often undeclared, beyond one's main job
slang for a lover kept in addition to a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Someone's extra income goes on keeping a mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both a secondary income and an illicit lover outside a marriage.

clue.text: Composer has a short time in Italian city

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer
MO is short for moment, a brief time

explanation.surface: A composer spends a brief stay in an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lombard city in northern Italy, near Milan.

clue.text: Pleased to reveal how trout might have been killed?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for delighted or thrilled

definitions.text: how trout might have been killed?
definitions.meaning: trout tickling is a poaching method of stroking a fish until it can be flicked out of the water

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to explain how a fish met its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hugely delighted, and taken literally it describes a fish dying after being caught by stroking.

clue.text: New employment right is introduced for care worker

indicators.note: the letter for right is introduced into the run made by the other pieces

parts.note: employment of something is its use

explanation.surface: A new job rule brings in a right for care staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after the sick in hospital or at home.

clue.text: Festival in which drink is restricted, so we hear

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: hock is a German white wine and tied means restricted

explanation.surface: A celebration where alcohol is rationed, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK (a German white wine) plus TIED (restricted) sounds like the festival. Hocktide was an old English festival held after Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English holiday celebrated in the week after Easter.

clue.text: Wound lover boy up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eros is the Greek boy-god of love

explanation.surface: An instruction to wind up a romantic young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore is a painful raw spot on the body, such as an injury.

clue.text: LSD's principally available in night clubs, journalist revealed

indicators.note: places the selected letter within the word for night clubs

parts.note: discos are night clubs for dancing

indicators.note: means the leading letter of the drug's name is taken

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter reveals that the drug is freely on sale in night clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Disclosed means made known or exposed.

clue.text: Stone corrupt cardinals in s. Pacific location

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to stone corrupt cardinals somewhere in the South Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges CARDINALS plus IN into CAIRNISLAND. 'Stone' looks like a verb but it is the noun PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote British island territory in the southern Pacific Ocean, settled by the Bounty mutineers.

clue.text: After short dramatic scene, thespian finally entered the stage

indicators.note: places the final letter of the actor's word after the scene

parts.note: a cameo is a brief role or scene in a play

indicators.note: means the closing letter of thespian is taken

explanation.surface: After a brief scene, the actor at last made an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To come on is to make an entrance before the audience.

clue.text: Bike brought back on motor vehicle

indicators.note: means the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
a car is a motor vehicle

explanation.surface: A bicycle is returned on top of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is a lightweight bicycle built for speed.

clue.text: Queen of Sweden isn't a rich sort

indicators.note: used as a verb, to sort the letters is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A monarch who is not a wealthy type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun meaning type, but it is the instruction to rearrange ISNTARICH.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century Swedish monarch who abdicated and converted to Catholicism.

clue.text: At length, people inhabiting small islands will make complaints

indicators.note: the letters for length and people live inside the islands word

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
men are people

explanation.surface: Eventually, folk living on tiny islands will grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: An AIT (or eyot) is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments are illnesses, the kind of complaints a doctor treats.

clue.text: Hit it off mostly with male? Nothing new in that, so to speak

definitions.text: Nothing new in that, so to speak

indicators.note: means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: two people who hit it off click
HE is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Getting on well with a man is nothing original.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed phrase is one with no originality left in it.

clue.text: Lord wearing medal offers assistance to some women

indicators.note: the decoration is worn around the lord, so his letters go inside it

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
to aid is to offer assistance

explanation.surface: A decorated peer helps out some women.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmarried older women were once called spinsters or this dated phrase.

clue.text: Answer question artist raised over French woman's painting technique

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are turned upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A question about an artist going over a Frenchwoman's painting method.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercolour painting technique using transparent washes.

clue.text: One's very much bowled over by an Irish poet

indicators.note: knocked over, so the pair of words is turned backwards

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I, then IS
so means very much, as in so happy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is quite overwhelmed by a poet from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is I'S (I is), turned with SO by 'bowled over' to give OSSI. Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard whose poems Macpherson claimed to translate.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Gaelic bard, Oisin, of the Fenian cycle.

clue.text: Fellow labourer having pig initially replaced by bovine creature

indicators.note: the opening letter of the pig word is swapped out for another piece

parts.note: a porker is a pig fattened for meat
a cow is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A farmhand has a pig whose place is taken by a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is someone who works alongside you.

clue.text: Entering off-licence, for example, union members very quickly got high

indicators.note: the union letters go into the shop

parts.note: an off-licence is a shop selling alcohol to take away
TU stands for trade union, whose members

explanation.surface: Union men burst into a liquor store and quickly got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is the British name for a liquor store.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise sharply in a short time, like prices or a growing child.

clue.text: Spy a fellow's brought in as a plant

indicators.note: the name is brought inside the word for spy

parts.note: to spy is to see
Sam is a man's name, so a fellow; the 's is is

explanation.surface: Espionage: an agent is planted as a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil-seed plant grown for its small seeds.

clue.text: One who doesn't object as city dweller has doubled capital?

indicators.note: the initial letter, a Roman numeral, is replaced by the numeral for twice its value

parts.note: a Londoner lives in a city

explanation.surface: A capital resident lets something pass, having two capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: L is Roman 50; doubled it becomes C, 100, so the first letter of LONDONER changes from L to C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who overlooks or forgives wrongdoing rather than protesting.

clue.text: Oven-ready bird daughter removed from car

indicators.note: the daughter's letter is taken out of the car

parts.note: a roadster is an open sports car

explanation.surface: A girl is taken out of a car with a chicken ready for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken suitable for roasting rather than boiling or frying.

clue.text: Wind is rare in mountain area

indicators.note: as a verb, to wind is to twist, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A breeze is uncommon in the highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' reads as a noun, a breeze; it is the verb (rhymes with mind) that rearranges ISRARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain range.

clue.text: Lady associated scam with obsolete savings scheme

parts.note: a con is a swindle
TESSA, the Tax Exempt Special Savings Account, was a UK savings scheme withdrawn in 1999

explanation.surface: A woman is linked to a fraud involving a defunct savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian countess, a titled noblewoman.

clue.text: Story book kept inside an item of furniture

indicators.note: the book letter is kept within the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A storybook stored inside a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a common piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Obedient hound, perhaps, trained up to catch duck

indicators.note: the duck letter is caught inside the turned word
in a down clue, directed upwards means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a hound is one kind of dog
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A well-behaved hound, trained to catch a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained up' turns DOG into GOD, which catches O. 'Obedient hound' looks like one phrase but only 'Obedient' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Good means well-behaved, like a compliant child or pet.

clue.text: Tom walker botched school subject, once

indicators.note: something botched is messed up, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A man called Tom has walked badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft subject once commonly taught in British schools, shaping metal.

clue.text: Creature fished from Danube, astonishingly

indicators.note: the letters are pulled out of the words like a fish from a river

explanation.surface: An astonishing creature caught in the Danube.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is an animal.

clue.text: He/she has good one to finish drinking bout

parts.note: an ender is one who ends something
a bender is a drinking spree

explanation.surface: A man or woman who finishes a binge well.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who blurs or crosses gender lines, playfully suggested by the slash form.
